A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SOC research, with matching authors, methods, and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including v4's expanded galleries.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection, segmentation, grounding, and intra-class referring experiments, component and scaling ablations, FID measurements, and a human assessment of 200 synthetic segments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and additionally provides numerical Subject200K comparison results and object-size-specific AP values in Appendix D.1, Table 7.

M1.justification: The object-generation, 3D placement, harmonization, blending, camera-augmentation, and annotation procedures remain the same. Appendix E.2–E.3 expands their documentation; the newly disclosed depth-map implementation does not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: The evaluated datasets, tasks, and SOC variants are retained. Subject200K was already discussed as an evaluated segment source in v2. The appendix's vocabulary count changes from 47K+ to 46K+, aligning with the existing main-text description without identifying a changed category set.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the main experiments is unchanged. v2 Appendix D.1 already reports a size-matched Mask2Former comparison against Subject200K; v4 supplies numerical scores for that comparison rather than introducing an entirely new comparator.

E3.justification: v4 Table 7 adds small-, medium-, and large-object AP metrics to the segment-source comparison. Existing training schedules, evaluation splits, and principal metrics are retained. The augmentation probabilities and execution timing are newly disclosed details, rather than established changes to previous settings.

E4.justification: Table 7 extends segment-quality analysis with object-size breakdowns for real-only, real-plus-Subject200K, and real-plus-SOC training. The existing component ablations, scaling study, FID analysis, and human segment-quality assessment remain unchanged. The new galleries primarily illustrate outputs rather than introduce robustness tests.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-training uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the reported comparisons. The existing generation-seed information and human-study sample count are unchanged; the new results follow the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 Table 7 newly reports Subject200K at 12.06 AP against SOC's retained 12.79 AP, a 0.73-point difference, and adds size-specific scores for all three segment-source settings. Main benchmark values, component ablations, scaling results, FID scores, and the 92% human-quality finding are retained.

T1.justification: The category-independence formulation, perspective projection, circle-of-confusion formula, and blending equations are unchanged. v4 repeats existing mathematics in expanded procedural explanations and removes some equation numbering, without adding formal results, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims concerning scalable synthetic composition, complementarity with real data, and targeted intra-class referring. The additional comparison evidence supports an existing claim.

C2.justification: New Appendix E.2 distinguishes harmonization's removal of visual artifacts from layout randomization's suppression of statistical shortcuts, and suggests photorealistic layouts may harm robustness. Appendix D.3 shortens the earlier categorical interpretation of realism versus annotation quality. The explicit limitations in Appendix A are unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 discloses independent 30% probabilities for zoom and blur, Depth Anything V2 depth prediction with rescaling and replacement by sampled object depths, and on-the-fly camera augmentation during training. These improve implementation documentation; existing hardware, training schedules, prompts, and resource-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The Harlequin bibliography entry is removed, while X-Paste remains represented by its retained reference. Most other bibliography changes revise metadata for the same named works. The positioning against simulator, copy-paste, and diffusion-based approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits concentrate on condensing Appendix D, adding step-by-step explanations in E.2–E.3, introducing gallery sections, and cleaning up terminology and bibliography entries. The main narrative remains essentially verbatim, so this is a localized revision rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 adds extensive galleries showing 100 object segments and ten annotated training images, two camera-augmentation figures, and the quantitative Subject200K table. Existing appendix figures and tables are retained but rearranged and renumbered, while main plots receive limited styling and label updates. This substantially expands the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the previously qualitative Subject200K comparison numerically auditable and supplies useful augmentation details, improving evidential completeness and reproducibility. The galleries improve inspectability, although they contain inconsistencies: the rice-cooker example assigns a machine-gun expression the tablecloth's box. The main evidence is otherwise unchanged, and the stronger robustness interpretation lacks a new robustness test, so the net improvement is limited.
